subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The difference between weather and climate is that weather is:
options: The day-to-day state of the atmosphere; climate is the long-term average
questions.explain: Weather is short-term; climate is the average conditions over many years.
A rain gauge measures precipitation; a thermometer measures temperature.
An anemometer measures wind speed; a barometer measures pressure.

options: Cloud, rain and windy, changeable weather
questions.explain: Depressions bring unsettled weather; anticyclones (high pressure) bring calm, clear conditions.

questions.q: An anticyclone (high pressure) in summer typically brings:
questions.explain: High pressure brings sinking air, clear skies and calm conditions.

questions.q: An example of extreme weather in the UK is:
questions.explain: Extreme weather events are unusually severe and can cause damage.

questions.q: Evidence that climate is changing includes:
options: Rising global temperatures and shrinking ice sheets
questions.explain: Warming, ice melt and sea-level rise provide evidence of climate change.

questions.q: A weather forecast predicting rain, wind and falling pressure suggests the approach of a:
questions.explain: Falling pressure and unsettled conditions indicate an approaching depression.

options: Non-living factors such as climate, water and soil

questions.q: A tropical rainforest is characterised by:
options: Hot, wet conditions and very high biodiversity
questions.explain: Rainforests have high temperatures, heavy rainfall and rich biodiversity.

questions.q: Plants in a hot desert are adapted to:
options: Reduce water loss, e.g. with spines and deep or wide roots
questions.explain: Desert plants (xerophytes) minimise water loss and maximise water uptake.

options: Cold, with low temperatures and little vegetation
questions.explain: Tundra is cold, with permafrost and sparse, low-growing vegetation.

questions.q: Nutrient cycling in a rainforest is rapid because:
options: Warm, wet conditions cause fast decomposition
questions.explain: Heat and moisture speed decomposition, recycling nutrients quickly.

questions.q: In a food chain, the arrows show:
questions.explain: Arrows point from the organism being eaten to the consumer, showing energy transfer.

options: The variety of living organisms in an ecosystem
questions.explain: High biodiversity indicates a rich variety of species.

questions.q: Deforestation of a rainforest is likely to:
options: Reduce biodiversity and disrupt nutrient cycling
questions.explain: Clearing forest destroys habitats and releases stored carbon.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE Geography A specification; Weather, climate and ecosystems
